1.bug_scenario: The issue is that the Checkbox component does not support a read-only state. When you pass in readOnly={true} (as in the reproduce code), the input still looks and behaves like an enabled checkbox. The design spec calls for a specific “read-only” style (different border/text color, spacing, and no pointer cursor) but none of the implementation files (component, styling, stories, docs, or tests) have been updated to handle this new prop/class.

2.explanation: • Checkbox.tsx – this is the core component.  It needs to accept a new readOnly prop, conditionally append a ‘--readonly’ (or similar) class to the outer wrapper, and pass through any custom className.  • Checkbox.stories.js – we must add a new story and controls for the readOnly prop so designers and developers can preview and copy/paste usage.  • Checkbox-test.js – the existing unit/RTL test should be updated (or a new one added) to render the component with readOnly=true and assert that the correct class is present on the DOM node.  • _checkbox.scss – under the React package’s scss/components/checkbox folder we need to write the actual styles for the read-only modifier (neutral border for unchecked, primary outline for checked, correct spacing and no hover/focus background).  Together these files implement the missing API, visuals, docs, and tests for the read-only checkbox variant.
2.bug_scenario: The bug here is that the React Checkbox component doesn’t support a read-only variant.  Although consumers can pass a readOnly prop and even a helper className, the component’s code never applies a special class or styles for a “read‐only” state, so the checkbox always renders as an interactive, enabled control.  According to the design specs (see the two images)—• unselected read‐only boxes must use a neutral border color and not fill on hover/focus, • selected read‐only boxes must use the primary icon color with a transparent background, • spacing between the box and label must match the spec—none of that is implemented.  To fix this, we need to: 1) extend the Checkbox component API to accept and apply a readOnly prop, 2) add the corresponding CSS/Sass rules under the react package’s scss folder, 3) add stories and controls so consumers can play with the state in Storybook, and 4) add a RTL/unit test to verify the read‐only class appears when readOnly=true.
